Hi Priyom —

Thanks for sending this over. Tom and I reviewed and added a few redlines (see attached PDF). High-level notes:

1) The quote on page 2 is fine but please change "reduced inference cost by 40%" to "reduced token inference costs by ~40% in peak workloads" — that qualifier is important for our procurement team.
2) The latency metric on page 3 shows 85ms average; our internal measurement for the same workload is closer to 110ms. Can you confirm which window/version this came from?
3) Please remove the paragraph about "no PII retention" on page 4 — we need a legal-approved privacy statement (we will send our standard line).

I'm attaching our marked-up PDF (Keystone_Redlines_v1.pdf). If you can incorporate these changes and return a Rev A, we'll aim to sign off within 48 hours.

Best,

Priyom —

Thanks for flagging. My take:

- Use Keystone's 110ms number with an explicit attribution: "Keystone Health internal measurement, May 2027 (search workload)." That keeps the case study truthful and avoids a footrace over benchmarks. If we want to show Redwood's baseline, put it in a separate paragraph with our method note.
- For the privacy sentence, propose this short line: "Redwood processes customer data in accordance with contract terms and customer-configured retention policies; no data is used for model training without explicit customer consent." It's generic but legal-friendly. If Rachel thinks it's ok, send the Rev A with both the attribution and the privacy blurb.

I can also do a quick editorial pass on the quote wording to add the qualifier Elena requested.
